title: Windows Support I
subject: Windows Fundamentals
description: 8 gamified support tickets focused on Windows installation, disk storage, local accounts, and file sharing. Use the 4-step workflow to document your findings and actions.

tickets.title: User cannot copy a large file to a USB drive
tickets.summary: A user reports 'Not enough space' when copying a single large file to a USB drive that appears to have free space.

env.Impact: User cannot transfer a required file

triage.q: Capture symptoms and scope. What is the exact error? What is the file size? What does Windows show as free space?
options: Apply a random fix based on guesswork with no validation.
Assume it is a user mistake and close the ticket.
Confirm scope and capture exact symptoms/error text before acting.
Reboot immediately without collecting any details.

diagnosis.q: State your most likely root cause and the evidence you will use to confirm it.
options: Rely only on user opinion rather than measurable evidence.
Skip diagnosis and go straight to changes on production systems.
Form a likely root cause and identify specific evidence to confirm or rule it out.
Blame the network without checking any logs or configuration.

fix.q: Document the GUI steps you will take to resolve it (and what you will verify after).
options: Apply the least-risk remediation, then verify the service is restored and document results.
Make multiple changes at once so you cannot isolate what fixed it.
Disable security controls to make the problem go away.
Declare success without testing or validation.

workflow.changeNote: Write a change record: what changed, why, impact, and validation.

validations: Verify the solution matches user constraints (data retention, tool limitations)

debrief.summary: You recognized that large-file copy failures to USB often trace back to filesystem limitations (e.g., FAT32 max file size) rather than Windows permissions or "broken" USB media.
debrief.takeaway: Match the storage format to the workload—use exFAT/NTFS when file sizes exceed FAT32 limits.

diagnosis.q: State your likely root cause and the evidence you will use to confirm it (BIOS/UEFI checks, disk state, etc.).

Form a likely root cause and identify specific evidence to confirm or rule it out.

options: Disable security controls to make the problem go away.

debrief.summary: You tied Windows Setup disk selection failures to storage configuration (wrong partition style, missing storage driver, or disk offline/uninitialized) instead of assuming the installer is corrupt.
debrief.takeaway: When Setup can’t see a disk, validate BIOS/UEFI mode, disk partition style (GPT/MBR), and storage drivers first.

debrief.summary: You identified that a newly attached disk won’t appear in File Explorer until it’s initialized, partitioned, and formatted. Disk Management is the first stop for visibility issues.
debrief.takeaway: Windows requires a volume (partition + filesystem + drive letter) before a disk shows up to users.
